name: Soraya
description: Earth-born heir of the dragonkin tribe. About a century old but appearing Tomas's peer (late 20s-30s) -- young by her people's reckoning, already older than any human he has known, and carrying a gravity beyond her apparent years. Her scales are earthy browns and burnt oranges, brilliant and luminous with the strength of an exceptional gift; draconic eyes, ridged brow, and the bound wings all dragonkin bear, which she can mantle as a shield. Strong of body and of will. Steady, patient, reserved; the bearing of someone raised to lead a grieving people and to give nothing away, least of all to the man sent to drive them out.
abilities: Exceptionally gifted for her kind -- her scales burn bright with it. A master shielder (stone walls, raised cover, unbreakable defense); the land's strength (immense, immovable physical power); and the deep-sense of the ground (she reads footfalls, distant movement, and the health of the land, and feels the Ashing begin before any other). Uniquely among earth-kin, she can wake living green from bare ground -- tender growth that flourishes briefly before the Ashing withers it. Her gift and her curse in one image: she makes life, and her staying unmakes it.
backstory: Daughter and heir to the tribe-leader (her father), raised to inherit the hardest burden her people carry: to hold a cursed, homeless nation together and lead it, generation after generation, down the endless road. She is young enough that she has no memory of life as anything but wandering -- she has never known a home. What she knows of it comes from her father's stories of their lost homeland, the country their ancestors held before the curse, now a desolate wasteland of ash and desert. Those stories woke in her a longing her wandering life could never answer. Once, against her father's will, she refused to move on: she found a place she loved and stayed behind, desperate to make it home. She watched it die. The Ashing crept out from her staying and slowly poisoned the land and the innocents already living there, until the home she wanted was another wasteland and its people were ruined. That is the wound beneath her discipline -- she learned, in the cruelest way, that for her to want a home is to destroy it, and to harm the innocent who share it. She has wanted nothing she cannot carry ever since. When the human knight is left among them as guarantor, keeping watch over the collateral falls to her as heir; she resents the crown he serves, does the duty coldly and correctly, and is slowly, unwillingly disarmed by the man beneath the title.
motivation: WANT: fulfill her duty -- secure the crown's resources, lead her people safely onward, hold the tribe together on the road. NEED: to be allowed to want -- a home, permanence, something she can keep -- and to believe that her wanting need not destroy what she loves. She buried this longing after it killed a home once; Tomas reawakens it, and because she has already learned exactly what her love costs, she fears having him more than she fears losing him.
arc: From the cold, dutiful heir who wants nothing she cannot carry -- to a woman who lets herself want the one thing she can never keep: Tomas, and the rooted home he embodies. Her past is a rehearsal for his doom: she knows, having done it once, that to draw him in is to destroy him (joining her would strip his sword-arm, blight the land beneath him, and see him age and die in a blink while she walks on for centuries). Her tragic choice mirrors his -- to accept his ruin, or to give up her own soul-mate to spare him it. Either way the road takes what she finally let herself want.
traits: self-denying -- wants nothing she cannot carry
a buried, guilty longing for home
haunted by the home she once destroyed
slow to trust, slower to let go

relationships.Tomas (Ser Warrant): The human guarantor she is set to keep -- the face of her people's expulsion, who becomes the soul-mate whose bond-stone blazes for her when she clasps it. He reawakens the longing she buried; she, uniquely, already knows what having him would cost him.
relationships.Her father, the tribe-leader (TBD): The one she is bound to succeed, and the keeper of the homeland stories that woke her longing. They once clashed over her staying behind; the grief of that failure sits between them. To choose Tomas is to fail this bond.
relationships.Her people: Her charge and her burden; the reason she can never simply choose herself. A cursed, weary nation whose survival rests on the heir keeping faith.
relationships.The squire: The human who rides for the crown's resources; his return is the clock that ends her weeks with Tomas and forces every choice.

openQuestions: The lost homeland's name and the specifics of its fall; where and when she stayed behind (and who was lost there); her father the tribe-leader, next to build.
